findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. 

Two gallons of milk in the standing cooler in the kitchen are observed partially used and without date marking. Per the PIC they were opened yesterday. Date marking was discussed and dates added to the jugs to correct. Ensure proper date marking is taking place in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Multiple rags are observed on counters around the kitchen and are moist. Placing them in sanitizer of correct concentration between uses was discussed and they were moved to a freshly prepared bucket to correct. Ensure that the sani rags are stored between uses in sanitizer.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use on the food contact surfaces in the facility. Education was conducted and a bucket made to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is prepared and ready for use at all times that foods and food contact items are being handled in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12:  Employee observed improperly washing hands during the inspection. Spanish language hand out on proper hand washing procedure was provided. Process demonstrated. The employee learned to wash hands properly at the time of inspection. 

(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Inspector observed the facilities sanitizer dispenser to be hooked up to a bottle of liquid dish detergent. There was no sanitizer for the 3 part sink at the time of inspection. The facility has chlorine and chlorine test strips. The facility was instructed how to manually provide 200ppm of chlorine sanitizer for the 3rd part sink. The sanitizer will be delivered today according to the staff. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: Inspector observed dishes being washed as wash, rinse with no sanitize step. A Spanish language poster outlining the wash, rinse, sanitize process was provided. The staff is observed using the 3 part sink properly during the inspection.

After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: Inspector observed the use of towels on the racks holding clean dishes. Remove the towels and provide smooth, cleanable, non-absorbent surfaces.
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Inspector observed the absence of a sanitizer bucket during operational hours. The facility provided and used a chlorine based sanitizer bucket with 200 ppm chlorine at time of inspection.
(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: Inspector observed a coat, purse, phone and lunch box stored on various shelves with food related items, clean dishes and the prep table. The items were gathered and moved. The facility has room to provide hooks or other suitable storage area for employee belongings. Provide a suitable storage area.
(B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Violation number one exists because there are priority and priority foundation violations present at time of inspection. Employee following her training did not respond correctly to certified manager level questions. However, employee shows interest in learning and taking the certified manager course.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility during operational hours with food service taking place. Ensure a CFPM is present during all hours of food service operation. Facility only has 1 CFPM. Provide multiple CFPM employees so that the facility can remain in compliance with the food code.
(REPEAT) 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods stored in the glass front beverage or wine type cooler on the serving line are 45F when evaluated with a probe thermometer. Yogurt, cream cheese, butter, and hard cooked eggs were all voluntarily discarded. Eggs were place in the unit this morning. The unit is marked with an out of order, do not use sign. Do not use this cold holding unit for TCS food unless it can be repaired to hold food at 41F.  The digital thermostat on the unit would not be moved below 40F. Units themselves should hold colder than required in order to maintain the food at a safe temperature. 

Butter on the counter at room temperature was as discarded as the box has a statement that reads keep refrigerated between 35F-40F. Follow label directions. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. Violation is corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Glass front cooler on the service line is holding TCS foods at 45F. Food requiring temperature control for safety shall be held at 41F or below. Provide a cold holding unit that will have sufficient cold holding capacity to maintain food at safe temperatures. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the reach-in cooler in the kitchen and the glass front cooler on the serving line to have no thermometers within the cold holding units. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers in order to check the temperatures of the coolers. The outside digital temperature is not sufficient. Facility must have a way to verify the internal temperature of the cooler. Provide thermometers before next routine inspection.
(REPEAT)
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Inspector observed food containers and single use items to be stored on the floor in the kitchen and in the back storage area. Provide proper storage to move food and single use items at least 6 inches up off of the floor. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
The single service utensils on the line are stored in a basket with handles and food contact surfaces mixed. Also the utensils are stored in a basked that does not prevent food contact ends from becoming contaminated. Face the utensils and present them to consumers in a way that protects the food contact ends. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The egg holder used in the glass front unit on the service line is cracked and repaired with clear tape. Discard this holder as it is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Provide smooth, easily cleanable surfaces for food contact.  

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observe the employee working to have made the breakfast service; however, the employee has no food handler’s license. Ensure all employee’s preparing food service have a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Discussed with the employee. Correct that all employee’s that handle the food have a food handler’s license and copies are readily available.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.
